current.text: He is the projected starting point guard and the offensive hub in Chicago. The projected starting five is Giddey, Norman Powell, Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton.
Experts project him at about 33 to 34 minutes and about 23 usage.
Nikola Vucevic and Coby White are gone, which frees usage in Chicago.

Experts disagree on his usage. One says it will drop because no one is out in Chicago, and that Norman Powell may lead the team in usage. Another says Buzelis could be second in usage, ahead of Giddey.
Experts expect around 10 assists per game, helped by the exits of Coby White and Dosunmu. One expert wants him top three in assists per game.
He still needs to score around 15 to 16 points per game because the team lacks shooting.
His shooting dropped last season, mainly an odd drop in FT%. One expert says it could bounce back, another says it is unclear. His three-point shooting also needs to recover.
He dealt with ankle injuries last season.

Experts call his price fair in category leagues: an end of round two or early round three pick, with ADP in the low to mid 20s about right and Yahoo rank 18 borderline but okay. One mock drafter called him a strong pick at 24.
His ESPN rank of 36 is good value. One expert thinks he is probably a top 20 player.
In an auction mock draft he went for 29 USD. The expert bid up to 24 USD and did not see 29 USD as a bargain.
He is the only Bulls player paid over 20 million USD per year.
He faces the most pressure on the team if the season goes badly.
Chicago projects as a bad team, likely bottom 10, with about 32 wins predicted. The team lacks shooting, and a lineup with Claxton, Wilson and Giddey will have poor spacing.
Tiago Splitter is the new head coach, replacing Billy Donovan.
The Bulls should play a fast, up-tempo transition style.
The Bulls are thin. Losing a main player like Giddey would make depth a problem.
Chicago has 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (3-3-4) and 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum. The first 20 games are a tough stretch.
The front office signs older players on short deals and hopes to trade them, so roster changes during the season are likely.

durable.text: He is a reliable source of points, rebounds and assists, with very high rebounds and assists for a guard and possible double digit assists.
Assists are a league outlier and rebounds are far above other guards.
Turnovers are his weak category. He is a high-turnover passer and needs to lower them.
Experts disagree on his usage profile. Two call him a low usage player whose variance comes from percentages and steals. Another calls him a high-usage passer.
He shot about 37% and 36.5% from three over the last two seasons on low volume.
Rebounding and transition play are strengths.
Availability is a concern. He needs to play over 60 to 65 games.
He is worth more in points leagues than in 9-cat. Experts see him as a top 20 points league player.

note: Giddey is an assist and rebound engine from a guard slot, but his turnovers are a league outlier, so he fits a punt TO build best. Yahoo values him at 37 USD (average cost 35 USD) and ESPN's average cost is 34 USD. He went for 31 USD in our league last season and 29 USD in a recent mock, so a price around 29 to 32 USD is fair for us. Early in the season, check his FT% and FG% (he projects at 45.3% FG and 77.1% FT), whether Powell or Buzelis takes usage from him, and whether he stays healthy after missing 28 games last season.
